verdicts.why: 'go' is the lemma of 'to go'/'take' LEGO 連れて行く; seed has 'take my mother to the doctor', so 'go' is an inflection/part of the LEGO, not an orphan.
'を' is the object marker inside LEGO 男性を ('man who'); the seed 'an old man who wanted' renders no separate object marker.
'I don't understand' glosses わかりません inside its own LEGO, but the seed says 'I'm not sure if it's true'; the row paraphrases the seed's chunk.
'do' glosses して in 〜していただけますか ('can you'); seed 'can you tell me what your name is?' has no 'do'.
'okay' glosses いい in してもいい ('do you mind if'); seed 'Do you mind if I ask you some questions?' has no 'okay'.
'before' glosses 前 within LEGO 前に ('earlier'); seed says 'talking about earlier', not 'before'.
'earlier' glosses 前に, but the seed's 'before I have to go' renders it as 'before'; the row is about its own sentence.
'(object)' is a marker gloss for を in LEGO を知っている ('who knows'); the seed 'a young woman who knows your sister' renders no object marker.
'previously' glosses 以前 in LEGO 以前〜していた ('used to'); the seed 'used to work' does not contain 'previously'.
'(marker)' glosses を in the seed's 'what you were doing' chunk, which renders no object marker.
'as it is' is a literal gloss of ながら inside 残念ながら ('unfortunately'); the seed has only 'unfortunately'.
'leave' is the lemma of 'left' in the seed ('you left them at work').
'not at all' glosses 全然 inside the idiom 'I don't have the faintest idea'; row is about its own sentence.
'long' glosses 中 in 一日中 ('all day'); the seed 'speak English all day' does not contain 'long'.
'doing (from やる, to do)' is an annotated lemma-style gloss of 'doing' in the seed 'you're doing very well'.
'looking for (from 探す, to search)' is an annotated gloss of 'looking for' in the seed 'what are you looking for?'.
'see (potential)' carries a grammar annotation; the seed 'I can't see' contains 'see' but the row text is not a clean substring.
'of course (part 1)' is a split-word gloss of もちろん; the seed contains 'of course', so it belongs to its own sentence.
'of course (part 2)' is a split-word gloss of もちろん; the seed contains 'of course', so it belongs to its own sentence.
'(subject marker)' glosses が in 方がいい ('should'); the seed 'I should consider...' renders no marker.
